tools.name: create_vibescape
tools.description: Use this when somebody wants a music visualiser or music visualisation (visualizer, visualization, musicviz, audio-reactive visuals): it writes a GLSL vibescape and returns a live link to it. The link draws and animates the vibescape in a browser, so it works for anybody who opens it, with or withou

tools.name: share_vibescape
tools.description: Use this when a vibescape should be listed in the public gallery, where anybody can find it at vibresia.com/vibescapes. A vibescape is created unlisted; this is the separate act of putting it in front of people. The name and the author go with it, so make sure they are right before calling this. Onl

tools.name: list_vibescapes
tools.description: Use this when somebody wants to see music visualisations other people have made, or wants something to look at before writing their own. Returns the public gallery: each vibescape's name, who made it, and a link that plays it.

tools.name: get_vibescape
tools.description: Use this to read somebody's vibescape, so it can be adapted or understood. Needs the id — the last part of the link.

tools.name: lint_vibescape
tools.description: Use this after writing a vibescape, before sharing it. It reads the code and says what would make it look wrong — most often that it never reads the music, so the picture is the same in silence as at full volume. Cheap to call and it catches most of what goes wrong.

tools.name: vibescape_reference
tools.description: Use this before writing a vibescape: it lists every uniform the music drives and every helper the language has, with what each is for. Writing a vibescape without it usually takes two attempts instead of one.

tools.name: get_palette
tools.description: Use this to find out how a vibescape's colours are graded. Vibresia puts every vibescape through one of five palettes, so bright colours come out muted unless the shader accounts for it.

tools.name: get_app
tools.description: Use this when somebody wants the real thing: the app listens to the system audio directly, with no browser, and checks for updates for you. It gives the download link and the one-line install command for macOS.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "share_vibescape" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
